evidence.note: Load: symbolic-ref exit 1 -> rebasing head-name; any other git failure leaves known=false so Classify puts everything in scope (fails closed)
case fold only when refs/heads/<spelling> resolves; non-1 failure leaves scope unknown
isRemoteDefault anchors refs/remotes/<one-segment>/main|master; rev-list base..HEAD --not <remoteDefaults> -- is valid with an empty list
Classify: unknown -> InScope; name/former-name leg, range leg, legacy leg (pastHeads or reachable), then OtherBranch/Orphaned
reachable: only merge-base exit 1, or rev-parse --verify exit 1 on a pruned commit, proves unreachable; cached per head

fsm init: symbolic-ref exit 1 = detached, other failures ERR_GIT; --for-branch validated against for-each-ref exact names and canonically against the checked-out branch; Branch passed to machine.InitOptions

MainWorktreeIsBare removed along with its test; its only base caller (internal/status/fsmruns.go bareMain, #174) was replaced by scope classification in this branch (git grep at ce80bb4 finds no Go callers); go build ./... and go vet pass
go test ./internal/scope ./internal/repo passes at head ce80bb4; prompt.go driver contract documents --for-branch consistently with run.go parseArgs

findings.note: Inconsistent fail-open in fsm init's case fold: run.go treats ANY rev-parse --verify failure (timeout, spawn error, exit 128) as 'do not fold' and records HEAD's spelling as-is, whereas scope.Load treats a non-1 failure as unknown. On a case-insensitive FS with a mis-cased checkout AND a transient git failure, the run is recorded under a spelling status never lists, so once its head leaves the range it reads as orphaned instead of blocking. Requires two unusual conditions at once; a follow-up could return gitFailed for code != 1 as the other git calls in init do.
readReflog uses a value receiver to fill maps (works because maps are reference types); already listed as accepted style in the fourth-round known list.
